chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: Baby Dodds, the low hat and Ludwig and Slingerland
summary: They talk about Baby Dodds never using a sock cymbal and a story about Ludwig making him a foot cymbal.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Did you hear Baby Dodds back in those days?
Oh, yeah, Baby and I were good friends.
You know, we were talking last week about the low hat and the high hat.
Yeah, right.
And you said, you said, back then, you can do anything if the left foot was free.
Right.
But Baby never did use --
He never used one the whole time.

I read an interview that somebody did with Baby that has not been published. A guy down in New Orleans has it. And Baby claims that when he was working the Streckfuss line, that Bill Slingerland or whatever his first name was -- this had to be in the early '20s.
Old Man Slingerland.
Old Man Slingerland.
Yeah, right, right.
Came on the boat one day and said his had this idea for this invention, and he took Baby's shoe size, and he came back later with a low hat (unintelligible).
Yeah, right, right, right.
And Baby said he didn't like it and never used it before.
Right, right.
But that he was -- it was his foot size.
Yeah, that must have been Bill Ludwig, Old Man Ludwig.
It was Ludwig --
Slingerland wasn't in -- yeah, right.
Yeah, the Old Man.
Old Man, right, they were always inventing something, they were very instrumental in a lot of new contraptions for drums.
